2609.18328.title: Visual Compliance via Executable Safety Rule Entailment
2609.18328.paper_summary: Recent advances in LLMs and VLMs have enabled safety systems to reason beyond simple risk patterns toward more contextual and semantic safety concerns. However, as risk patterns continue to evolve and safety rules become more complex, existing training-based end-to-end safeguards face persistent challenges in adaptability and explainable reasoning over complex safety rules. To address these challenges, we propose GuardEn (Guarding by Safety Rule Entailment), an executable safeguard framework that decomposes safety policies into atomic propositions through Safety-Rule Compilation, modeling their composition as executable code. At test time, Scene-Grounded Execution instantiates these atomic propositions with contextual visual information derived from scene graphs, enabling rule-grounded and interpretable safety reasoning. Experiments on SafetyVisionBench demonstrate the effectiveness of programmable safeguard for complex visual safety assessment, achieving an average improvement of 9.8 F1 points over the strongest baseline.
2609.18328.paper_summary_zh: 最近在大型語言模型（LLMs）和視覺語言模型（VLMs）方面的進展，使得安全系統能夠超越簡單的風險模式，朝向更具情境性和語義性的安全關注。然而，隨著風險模式的不斷演變和安全規則的日益複雜，現有基於訓練的端到端安全防護面臨著在適應性和對複雜安全規則的可解釋推理方面的持續挑戰。為了解決這些挑戰，我們提出了GuardEn（通過安全規則推導進行保護），這是一個可執行的安全防護框架，通過安全規則編譯將安全政策分解為原子命題，並將其組合建模為可執行代碼。在測試時，場景基礎執行使用來自場景圖的上下文視覺信息實例化這些原子命題，實現基於規則的可解釋安全推理。在SafetyVisionBench上的實驗證明了可編程安全防護在複雜視覺安全評估中的有效性，平均提高了9.8個F1點，相較於最強基準。
